Lagged coefficients, Picard iteration and Newton methods have different convergence requirements. Viscoelasticity additionally needs stress history and cannot be modeled by viscosity alone. For generalized Newtonian viscosity, coefficients depend on strain. A lagged-coefficient iteration takes the current velocity guess, evaluates shear rate and viscosity, builds the linear viscous system, solves it, and repeats until both velocity change and nonlinear residual meet their criteria.

Numerical priorities are component-aware pressure, obstacle sampling and bounded liquid volume. Formal priority is connecting array assembly to the abstract model. Non-Newtonian stress, APIC and sparsity follow needed capability rather than the project's name.

A liquid state needs more than a smoke concentration. Its interface locates a liquid domain, its density supplies inertial mass, and its volume ledger records transport and sources. Changing the grayscale opacity coefficient does not produce a liquid. This chapter specifies an incompressible, immiscible Newtonian research model. Compressible flow, phase change and dissolved materials are separate extensions.

Density and viscosity have different roles. Density weights inertia; dynamic viscosity relates deformation rate to stress; kinematic viscosity controls a simple diffusion time scale. Treating a viscosity slider as an arbitrary velocity damping factor hides both the material units and boundary work. The first liquid research model is Newtonian, with positive density and nonnegative viscosity.

For \(D=(\nabla u+\nabla u^T)/2\), Newtonian stress is \(\tau=2\mu D\). Its power dissipation is \(2\mu D:D\geq0\). The cross derivatives matter: rigid rotation has zero symmetric strain even though velocity gradients are nonzero. A scalar component Laplacian is equivalent to the incompressible constant-viscosity interior equation only under the matching assumptions and boundary terms.

Generalized Newtonian and viscoelastic materials remain later research. A shear-dependent viscosity needs an admissible range and nonlinear residual; viscoelasticity needs history and its own stress evolution. The existing finite-budget nonlinear specification in Chapter 10 remains valid. This expansion does not quietly turn it into an implemented material law.

Dry Coulomb friction bounds a tangential force using normal contact force. Applying it to a liquid-solid wall is a separate constitutive assumption, not the default Newtonian no-slip boundary law. A penalty damping term likewise has its own units and finite-step dissipation. Label it as a numerical/constitutive choice if used. A single “stickiness” parameter cannot consistently identify all of these mechanisms.

# Constant-density Newtonian viscosity in the sealed box

This implementation companion adds a bounded Newtonian update to the existing transactional carrier/liquid facade. It supports a **fully filled sealed Cartesian box**, constant positive density rho, constant nonnegative dynamic viscosity mu, and stationary impermeable **free-slip** walls. Normal wall velocity is prescribed zero. Tangential viscous traction is zero; this is not a no-slip or adhesion model. Material units are rho in kg/m³, mu in Pa s = kg/(m s), and nu = mu/rho in m²/s.

Older native prose says at most seven iterations, and the frozen refusal diagnosis records seven residual checks. That ambiguity is real: the old controller computed seven Newton corrections but checked only the seed and the first six corrections. The candidate interprets the inherited iteration budget as a cap on Newton correction solves, consistent with shared CG update semantics and Chapter 10's declared frozen-coefficient solve budget. This is a documented controller-semantic/check-order repair for review, not a claim that the check count is identical.

For N=min(max_iterations,7), the candidate computes at most N Newton corrections and checks their final result once. There are at most N+1 unperturbed Newton residual checks, thus at most eight, using the unchanged 1e-13 gate. The additional validation is cancellable through the existing Iteration stage, so that callback can be visited N+1 times. Historical reported `iterations` remains the number of original loop passes: a converged seed reports one; a terminal success after N corrections reports N despite N+1 residual checks. Ordinary acceptance after k corrections reports k+1 passes/checks. It is not an exact correction count on all paths.

Each computed correction uses one main equation evaluation and six finite-difference equation evaluations. The terminal check adds one equation evaluation, giving 7N+1 counted Newton calls (maximum 50), within the unchanged 200-call budget. Acceptance separately evaluates the original equation at quadrature orders 16 and 32. These two calls were already excluded from the report's Newton counter. Therefore an accepted budget-three boundary path reports 22 Newton calls but performs 24 total `work.equation` evaluations; an accepted budget-seven boundary path reports 50 but performs 52. These totals exclude seed assembly and optional diagnostic-only observations; they are not total runtime or total linear-solve counts.

The source candidate's shorthand “without another ... solve” means **without another Newton correction solve** or Jacobian construction. An equation evaluation itself performs the existing 15-by-15 chart solves; the terminal evaluation adds their work. No claim of zero added chart solves is made.

Actual trace accounting is recorded in `evidence/solver-terminal-validation/budget-normal.json` and its identical optimized-mode output. All preexisting Newton/work/GCL/momentum/quadrature/third-component gates and memory reservations remain. Original coarse temporal failures and remaining finer refusals are retained; no general convergence or arithmetic-floor theorem follows.

For N=min(settings.max_iterations,7), the original loop checks the seed/previous correction and performs at most N corrections. If it has not converged, the candidate evaluates the already computed final correction once at quadrature order 16 and the existing Newton rate target 1e-13. The additional call is guarded by the existing 200-call budget and an Iteration cancellation barrier. No Jacobian or additional solve is permitted. Worst-case Newton equation calls are 7N+1 <=50, within 200. Independent order-16/order-32 acceptance evaluations, original 1e-15 quadrature gate, 1e-11 momentum gates, 128-epsilon work/GCL gates, original third-component solve and before-publication barrier all still execute. Their acceptance equations and tolerances are unchanged.

This changes a bounded native solver controller only. It supplies no new physical equation, free-surface pressure law, viscosity/adhesion/density model, surface reconstruction, arbitrary mesh family, full three-dimensional simulator, continuum convergence theorem or Lean kernel claim. Existing Jacobi fixtures, subnormal rejection, checked division, research failures and theorem limitations remain. Passing a terminal Newton test alone does not imply the remaining work/constraint/third-component gates pass. Candidate numerical captures and replay must be reported as new results with their exact source and unchanged physical gates, independently of the frozen failures.
